keyframe_review.note: 48,484 km2 for -1800..-1761: Larsa's, except Isin's own district until -1792 (contested -1797..-1792). The Isin page: Isin 'maintained its independence from Larsa for at least another forty years' after Enlil-bani (c. 1860), 'ultimately succumbing to Larsa's ruler Rim-Sin I'; its table lists Rim-Sin at Isin from c. 1792.

ledger.note: 2018 BCE: Ishbi-Erra makes Isin an independent kingdom. 'The First Dynasty of Isin was founded by Ishbi-Erra (r. 2018-1985 BCE)'; 'The province of Isin broke out and formed an independent kingdom under Ishbi-Erra'. His page: 'a man of Mari', an official of Ibbi-Sin, 'by Ibbi-Sin's 8th year' (c. 2021) 'assigning his own regnal year-names'. Nippur is this dossier's reading.

region.text: the north of Sumer beyond Isin and Nippur that Isin holds in the Isin-Larsa period (isin_-2008): the Cliopatria -2000 outline without Larsa, Ur, Lagash and Uruk

ledger.note: 2008 BCE (bridged): Isin takes the provinces around it. The Third Dynasty page: 'Subsequently, the provinces close to the center also became independent', 'this is well known for Eshnunna and especially Isin under the leadership of Ishbi-Erra, a renegade governor'; 'Ibbi-Sin managed to stay in power in Ur for about 20 years, controlling only a small portion of the empire he inherited'. The Ishbi-Erra page: after ousting the Elamite garrison from Ur he asserted 'suzerainty over Sumer and Akkad' (a later year-name). No page dates the growth; -2008 is third-dynasty-of-ur's date of the loss. The region is the part of that dossier's loss region (Sumer apart from Ur) that this dossier gives Isin; the rest (Larsa, Lagash, Uruk) is not Isin's in its keyframes.

region.text: Ur, from 'the Elamite who was dwelling in its midst'

ledger.note: 1983 BCE: Ishbi-Erra ousts the Elamite garrison from Ur. 'decisive victories against the Amorites in his 8th year and the Elamites in his 16th year', then 'Some years later' he 'ousted the Elamite garrison from Ur'; the Isin page's year-name: 'brought out of Ur, with his strong weapon, the Elamite who was dwelling in its midst'. The Shimashki page gives the occupation 21 years from 2004 (c. 1983); his 16th year would be c. 2002: the later figure is used.

1983 BCE (bridged): Ishbi-Erra holds Lagash province. The Larsa page: 'From there, Ishbi-Erra recaptured Ur as well as the cities of Uruk and Lagash'; the Isin page makes Gungunum 'the royally appointed governor of Larsa and Lagash province', so Lagash was Isin's to appoint. Neither page dates the recapture; it is placed with the Ur event of the same sentence, from nobody (third-dynasty-of-ur /ledger: Lagash stops using Ur's year names in -2024). Uruk is named by the Larsa page too but is not drawn (see notes).

region.text: Lagash province, under Gungunum as governor

ledger.note: 1932 BCE (bridged): Lagash province goes with Larsa's governor. Gungunum 'the royally appointed governor of Larsa and Lagash province' (Isin page; accession 1932 on the Gungunum page) 'broke with Isin' and took Ur later; the Gungunum page does not mention Lagash. The year is his accession. Mirror of larsa /ledger (gain of Lagash). The reviewer's point (Lagash did not pass from Isin to Larsa in -1906) is met: it passes here, and the loss of -1923 is Ur alone.

region.text: Ur, captured by Gungunum of Larsa 'to deliver a blow to Isin'

ledger.note: 1923 BCE: Gungunum of Larsa takes Ur. The Gungunum page: 'The exact year of Gungunum's capture of Ur cannot be determined with certainty, but the year names found so far suggest that it took place in either his seventh or his 10th year, i.e. 1926 or 1923 BC', and the tenth year-name 'is on the other hand definitely attested in Ur'; the later year is used. Larsa page: 'To legitimize his rule and deliver a blow to Isin, Gungunum captured the city of Ur.' [fixer me-01: re-dated from -1906 (bridged to Abisare) now that the Gungunum page dates it, confidence raised from 1 to 2; region trimmed from Ur and Lagash to Ur, Lagash being booked at -1932.]
1865 BCE: Nippur is lost. 'At some point, Nippur was also lost'; placed at the end of Sumuel's reign (c. 1894–1865), whose canal war the page describes. Year and taker bridged.

1860 BCE: Enlil-bani usurps Isin. 'Around 1860 BC, an outsider named Enlil-bani seized the throne of Isin, ending the hereditary dynasty established by Ishbi-Erra over 150 years earlier'; same state, same colour.
1797 BCE: Rim-Sin I invades Isin's territory. 'Around 1797 BC, he invaded the territory of Isin, finally seizing the capital around 1792 BC'.
1792 BCE: Isin falls; 'every year name of his rule after was named in years after the sack of Isin'.

1792 BCE: Rim-Sin I of Larsa takes Isin and ends the dynasty. 'finally seizing the capital around 1792 BC'; the Isin page: Isin 'ultimately succumbing to Larsa's ruler Rim-Sin I', its table listing Rim-Sin from c. 1792. Isin later fell to Babylon's Samsu-iluna in 1723 and the Second Dynasty of Isin (c. 1153–1022) ruled Babylonia: other states.

wars.name: Isin–Larsa rivalry
wars.outcome: Gungunum took Ur and broke with Isin; Abisare and Sumuel cut Isin's canals; Nippur was lost; Rim-Sin I invaded in c. 1797 and seized Isin c. 1792.
wars.note: The Larsa page gives no date for Gungunum's capture of Ur; Lipit-Ishtar (c. 1935–1924) and the 'Uruk–Isin–Babylon' coalition against Rim-Sin (undated on his page) are the other episodes.

wars.name: Expulsion of the Elamites from Ur
wars.outcome: Ishbi-Erra's victory over the Elamites in his 16th year and the later ousting of the garrison from Ur; Ur became Isin's.

certainty.note: City territories and canals, no surveyed border; the division of Sumer between Isin and Larsa is this dossier's reading of the pages.

notes:
Split from Cliopatria's 'Sumerian City-States' row: the kingdom of Isin, -2018..-1792, reviewing the -2000 and -1800 shapes with corrections that give it the north of Sumer. The pages are thin on territory: no page lists Isin's cities, so Nippur's adherence, the loss of Lagash to Gungunum's governorship (-1932) and of Ur to his capture (-1923) and of Nippur (-1865) are bridged at confidence 1 (Ur's capture is dated by the Gungunum page, confidence 2). Rim-Sin's own page dates Isin's fall c. 1792 (not the 1794 of some handbooks; no page opened gives 1794). Isin, Larsa are not in the gazetteer; Nippur, Ur, Lagash, Uruk are. Uruk's Sin-kashid dynasty (c. 1865–1802) and Eshnunna need dossiers (Isin-Larsa period; me-02 or a gap-filler).

ME-01 FIXES (after the review): (1) Growth from Isin and Nippur to the Cliopatria outline is booked: gain -2008 from third-dynasty-of-ur (bridged; the pages say 'the provinces close to the center also became independent ... especially Isin' without a year). third-dynasty-of-ur /ledger/11 loses 'Sumer apart from Ur', wider than this dossier's keyframes (Larsa, Lagash and Uruk are not Isin's here): that dossier's region should be trimmed to match (it is a fix-verdict dossier I did not touch). (2) K1 is split: isin_-2008 (-2008..-1984), isin_-1983 (with Ur and Lagash province, -1983..-1933), isin_-1932 (with Ur, -1932..-1924) and the Cliopatria shape from -1923. (3) Lagash: the Larsa page has Ishbi-Erra recapturing Ur, Uruk and Lagash, the Isin page makes Gungunum governor of Larsa and Lagash province, so Isin holds Lagash from -1983 (gain from nobody) and it passes to Larsa with Gungunum's accession in -1932; the -1906 loss now names Ur alone, re-dated to -1923 because the Gungunum page (opened for this fix) dates the capture to his 7th or 10th year (1926 or 1923). I disagree with the reviewer's reading that Lagash 'did not pass from Isin to Larsa': the governor was Isin's appointee, so the transfer is booked at his accession, not at the break. (4) Uruk: the Larsa page has Ishbi-Erra recapturing Uruk and the Gungunum page says Uruk 'had been held by Isin until the reign of Lipit-Ištar' with its status afterwards 'highly uncertain'; not drawn or booked (no date for either end), listed as a gap. (5) Nippur: the Gungunum page has Larsa ruling Nippur from Gungunum's 19th year (c. 1914) for a time, with Isin's reconquest undated; the ledger's -1865 loss ('At some point', Isin page) is kept and now looks too late for the first loss: a gap. (6) The Isin page does not claim Kish, Babylon or northern Babylonia for Isin, so K1's northern reach to Babylon's rise (c. 1894) and the buffer state of Kish remains unexplained by an event (the reviewer's thin item; Sumu-abum's page not opened).
